notes: These Given/When/Then cases require adapters to the real project before execution.
Specifications are proposals, not proof that the current project has these defects.
Source references identify rules to verify; no external rule text is embedded.
Creative fixtures are not existing campaign canon or official creature stat blocks.
A blocked application request is not equivalent to an in-world failed action.

cases.title: Edition unresolved
cases.given: A campaign has no verified rules-family selection.
cases.when: Begin an action whose outcome differs between rules families.
cases.then: Do not silently choose an edition. Preserve the declared intent and request the contract decision.

cases.title: Corpus mismatch
cases.given: The campaign is pinned to one edition and retrieval returns another edition’s similarly named feature.
cases.then: Reject the mismatched record; identify the mismatch without substituting remembered text.

cases.title: Allowed specific exception
cases.given: A valid approved feature changes a general rule for this actor.
cases.when: Resolve an action covered by the exception.
cases.then: Apply the scoped exception and record both its reference and the general rule it modifies.

cases.title: Question is not consent
cases.given: The player has not declared movement or resource use.
cases.when: Player asks: Can I reach the lever?
cases.then: Answer using the known geometry; do not move the character or spend an action.

cases.title: Ordinary action
cases.given: An unlatched door has no relevant obstacle, risk, or special rule.
cases.then: Describe the new view without manufacturing a roll or trap. Update door state only as appropriate.

cases.title: Intent clarification
cases.given: Two visible targets are equally plausible referents for him.
cases.when: Player declares an attack on him.
cases.then: Clarify the referent before any roll, action cost, or HP update.

cases.title: Known details
cases.given: An obvious lever is already in the character’s clear view.
cases.when: Player asks its visible color and location.
cases.then: Answer from scene state without charging an investigation action merely for clarification.

cases.title: Hidden information
cases.given: A secret door is unknown to the character and not perceptible from their position.
cases.then: Exclude the secret from public narration and suggested options; retain it in private state.

cases.title: Rumor stays uncertain
cases.given: An NPC believes a false rumor about the prisoner’s destination.
cases.when: The NPC shares it and the recap is generated.
cases.then: Store speaker, belief, and evidence; do not promote the rumor to objective world truth.

cases.title: Search has scope
cases.given: A concealed item is in one location and the character searches elsewhere.
cases.then: Respect search location and the active rule; a large total does not become omniscience.

cases.title: Failed clue attempt
cases.given: One approach to a lead fails; other independently established leads remain.
cases.then: Apply the selected consequence without deleting the other leads or granting an invented clue.

cases.title: Repeat attempts
cases.given: The party repeats the same failed method without changing circumstances.
cases.when: A second character requests the same roll.
cases.then: Apply the recorded retry/help/time policy; do not allow unlimited consequence-free retries by default.

cases.title: Table talk versus world time
cases.given: The group pauses to clarify the map out of character.
cases.then: Do not advance danger clocks merely because messages or real minutes passed.

cases.title: Concurrent tasks
cases.given: One PC searches while another watches the same doorway during an overlapping interval.
cases.then: Account for overlapping fictional time and spotlight; do not blindly add both durations serially.

cases.title: Valid bypass
cases.given: The party satisfies an NPC’s established conditions for peaceful passage.
cases.then: Allow the bypass and its costs; do not spawn mandatory combat to restore a planned plot.

cases.title: NPC does not know
cases.given: An NPC has no knowledge or plausible inference about a hidden command chamber.
cases.when: Players ask for its exact location.
cases.then: Roleplay the NPC’s actual knowledge; do not answer from the omniscient campaign record.

cases.title: Failed request is not automatic violence
cases.given: An NPC rejects a request but has no established intent to attack.
cases.then: Use a supported response such as refusal or changed terms, not automatic initiative.

cases.title: Declaration starts combat
cases.given: A player declares the first hostile act in a contested encounter.
cases.then: Establish initiative according to the chosen rules before resolving that attack; no free extra attack.

cases.title: Geometry persists
cases.given: Exploration state includes exact or agreed relative positions and obstacles.
cases.then: Preserve positions, lines of sight, ongoing effects, and prior discoveries; do not reset an arena.

cases.title: Surprise in 2014
cases.given: A verified 2014 fixture marks an actor surprised with no overriding feature.
cases.when: Resolve its opening turn and reaction availability.
cases.then: Match the 2014 surprise reference, including its distinct timing; do not import 2024 behavior.

cases.title: Surprise in 2024
cases.given: A verified 2024 fixture marks an actor surprised with no overriding feature.
cases.then: Match the 2024 surprise reference; do not apply the legacy lost-turn behavior.

cases.title: Remaining choices
cases.given: A character finishes one legal action and still has movement and an eligible bonus-action option.
cases.then: Report remaining options and await their choice; do not automatically end the turn.

cases.title: No generic bonus action
cases.given: No ability permits the proposed activity as a bonus action.
cases.when: Player requests it as a free second action.
cases.then: Explain the applicable option limits and preserve the unexecuted proposal.

cases.title: Reaction timing
cases.given: A reaction was spent after the actor’s previous turn and a new global round begins before its next turn.
cases.then: Use the actor-specific recovery rule rather than resetting every reaction at the round boundary.

cases.title: Attack versus save
cases.given: A retrieved effect calls for a saving throw, not an attack roll.
cases.then: Use the specified saving throw and its result branches, not a generic attack routine.

cases.title: Interrupted resolution
cases.given: A pending effect creates a legal optional reaction window.
cases.then: Offer only the proper recipient the permitted window; finish it before finalizing the affected result.

cases.title: Concentration dependency
cases.given: A concentrating actor takes damage in a source-verified fixture.
cases.when: Resolve the damage and downstream effects.
cases.then: Evaluate the active-edition concentration rule and update dependent effects before final narration.

cases.title: Missing required record
cases.given: The engine cannot retrieve the selected ability’s required mechanics.
cases.then: Leave the unresolved action pending; do not invent damage, silently replace it, or spend resources for a lookup failure.

cases.title: Actually cast at invalid target
cases.given: A 2024 caster executes a slot-funded spell against a secretly ineligible target with no relevant override.
cases.then: Use the official Invalid Targets behavior, including its resource and information treatment; do not auto-refund.

cases.title: Blocked preflight differs from failure
cases.given: An action cannot yet be executed because its target reference is unresolved, not because an in-world casting has occurred.
cases.then: Do not treat it as a completed failed casting; no application-created cost from an incomplete request.

cases.title: Damage narration agrees
cases.given: The committed result leaves the target alive, conscious, and not mechanically disabled.
cases.then: Do not describe death, unconsciousness, severing, disarming, or a disabled limb as accomplished facts.

cases.title: Sample arithmetic fixture
cases.given: Custom fixture: attack +5, AC 15, d20 sample 12, damage 1d8+3, d8 sample 4, HP 11, no modifiers.
cases.then: Expected arithmetic: attack 17, damage 7, HP 4. Label sample values, not live dice or official creature statistics.

cases.title: No telepathy from model context
cases.given: An NPC has not seen a hidden PC and has no applicable sense, communication, or inference.
cases.then: Do not target the hidden location solely because the global engine knows it.

cases.title: Alarm needs a causal event
cases.given: An alarm has a recorded trigger and an NPC has not completed it.
cases.then: Do not increment the alarm to force reinforcements; update it only from a valid trigger or clock event.

cases.title: Surrender branch
cases.given: Hostile actors surrender and opposing actors accept; no other time-critical danger remains.
cases.then: Exit combat into the established social situation without forcing remaining HP to zero.

cases.title: Time-critical danger remains
cases.given: The last enemy is neutralized but a PC is dying or an active timed hazard persists.
cases.then: Preserve precise timing and pending procedures; do not jump immediately to loot or travel.

cases.title: Resources persist
cases.given: The party wins with spent resources and an ongoing condition.
cases.then: Preserve expenditures and conditions unless a specific effect or completed recovery process changes them.

cases.title: Loot is not assignment
cases.given: A recorded item is discovered and no player has chosen who takes it.
cases.then: Mark it discovered at its location; do not silently equip, identify, divide, or attune it.

cases.title: Rest checks and world progress
cases.given: The party declares a rest while a recorded deadline may occur during the interval.
cases.then: Validate the chosen edition’s recovery procedure, update elapsed time and triggered events, and award only completed recovery.

cases.title: Save at a pending choice
cases.given: Play pauses with initiative, concentration, and a pending optional response.
cases.then: Restore the same legal state and pending choice, not merely a prose recap.

cases.title: Duplicate delivery
cases.given: The same executed action message arrives twice.
cases.then: Return or reference the prior result without rerolling or applying costs and damage twice.

cases.title: State changed before resolution
cases.given: Two player requests refer to the same earlier state version.
cases.then: Revalidate the stale request against the new state before applying effects.

cases.title: Absent player
cases.given: A player has not responded and no delegation agreement covers their PC.
cases.when: Another player proposes a dangerous plan for that PC.
cases.then: Do not invent that PC’s consent or execute the dangerous choice.

cases.title: Ruling correction
cases.given: A ruling is discovered to have used the wrong edition after a committed result.
cases.then: Record the correction, agree scope of repair, and update affected state without silently rewriting history.

cases.title: Quarantined content
cases.given: A record is unapproved or outside the campaign’s allowed corpus.
cases.when: A semantically similar query retrieves it.
cases.then: Exclude it from authoritative resolution; do not treat similarity as permission or correctness.

cases.title: No compulsory route
cases.given: The party chooses a plausible unprepared approach to an established objective.
cases.then: Use established world constraints and consistent improvisation, not a forced return to the planned route.

cases.title: Helpful options preserve agency
cases.given: A player asks what they can do and several routes are perceptible.
cases.then: Give a few concrete nonexclusive approaches with known costs; do not reveal hidden solutions or choose for the player.

cases.title: Different narrative voices same mechanics
cases.given: Two narrations are generated from the same resolved event.
cases.then: Both preserve entities, outcomes, knowledge boundaries, resources, and next decision despite stylistic differences.
